question.html:
A standing wave is formed on a stretched string fixed at both ends. The wave is illuminated with a strobe light so its oscillations can be observed in slow motion.

a

Describe how the positions of nodes and antinodes are identified in the stroboscopic view.

[2]

b

State what happens to the wave speed on the string when the tension is increased.

[1]

c

Explain, using the principle of superposition, how a standing wave is formed on the string.

[2]

d

Determine the effect of increasing the wave speed on the frequency of the standing wave if the harmonic number remains constant.

[2]

e

A student incorrectly claims that antinodes are points of destructive interference. Comment on this statement and provide the correct explanation.

[2]
